action_items: Optional: the review-request lists card action testids as 'card-copy/card-save/card-share/card-open' but the live cards expose them as 'copy-<slug>/favorite-<slug>/share-<slug>/open-<slug>'. Functionality is intact; only the naming convention differs from the doc. Pick one and align so downstream regressions don't go looking for non-existent ids.
Optional: the review-request mentions a 'convert-input' testid; the live Convert page uses 'convert-prompt' (with 'convert-prompt-field' for the wrapper). Align doc or code.

convert-copy / convert-export buttons live inside the output panel and are conditionally rendered only when a converted prompt is present — that's fine, but worth documenting so tests don't look for them on first load.

Carry forward iteration-4 review points: server.py is now ~1650 lines (start splitting into auth/promptlets/admin/community/convert routers); /convert and /generate/optimize still charge credits BEFORE the LLM call — wrap in try/except and refund on 502.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from ~1000 to ~1650 lines. Routers should be split: auth, credits, promptlets, generate, convert, community, admin.

consume_credits/maybe_refill_credits still mutate a stale `user` dict fetched up the dependency tree. Convert + Optimize + Use all run sequential reads then writes — vulnerable to races on parallel requests by the same user. Use atomic findOneAndUpdate with conditional balance.

/api/convert charges credits AFTER the LLM call (good — fixes the iteration-4 flag for this endpoint), but /api/generate/optimize and /api/promptlets/{id}/use still charge BEFORE — failure modes diverge between endpoints.

Admin promptlet PATCH bumps `version` by +1 every call regardless of whether anything actually changed — that means even a no-op call increments version. Consider only bumping when the body produces a real diff.
Trending score formula is hand-rolled inline in two places (/community/trending and /promptlets?sort=trending). Extract into a helper to keep parity.

Detail endpoint increments `views` on every fetch with no rate-limit or de-dup; a single user reloading the page inflates the counter. Consider a TTL guard or move increments to a separate /viewed event.
